solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Purple heads in magenta and emerald, absorbing ultraviolet

indicators.note: something absorbing another thing takes it inside itself, so one piece is placed within the other
the heads of words are their front letters, so only the opening letter of each following word is kept

parts.note: the first letters of magenta, and, emerald
UV is the standard abbreviation for ultraviolet

explanation.surface: A colour chemist describes a purple shade made from magenta and emerald pigments that soaks up ultraviolet light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads in' means the heads of the words that follow, not of the word 'in' itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Mauve is a pale bluish-purple shade, the dye that gave its name to a whole Victorian colour craze.

clue.text: Dressing lead actor in wet earth

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it, so these letters go within the next piece

parts.note: wet earth is mud
the lead actor in a film is its star

explanation.surface: A film's lead actor gets a coating of wet earth, a dressing for the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' suggests costume, but here it is the condiment, as in a salad dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustard is a sharp condiment used as a sauce or salad dressing, spread on meats and sandwiches.

clue.text: Trustworthy university shifted blame for pinching fruit

parts.note: uni is the everyday short form of university

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing and holding something tight, so one piece clasps another inside it
letters that are shifted are moved about, so this word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a peach is a fruit

explanation.surface: A university passes the blame onto someone else for stealing fruit, hardly the act of a trustworthy institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' looks like stealing in the surface, but it signals one piece held inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unimpeachable cannot be called into question or doubted, so they are wholly reliable and honest.

clue.text: Ruin of Memphis underlying European Union's inoffensive wording

indicators.note: in a down answer, lying under another piece means coming after it in the grid

parts.note: EU is the abbreviation for European Union

indicators.note: a ruin of something is that thing wrecked, so the letters of this city are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: the city name taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A diplomatic note about the ruins of ancient Memphis, beneath EU bureaucracy, couched in soft inoffensive wording.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphemism is a mild or indirect expression substituted for one considered too harsh or blunt.

clue.text: Imitator of police officer and unknown jazz fan?

parts.note: a cop is a police officer
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns
cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast

explanation.surface: A mysterious figure who copies a police officer and an anonymous jazz lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A copycat is someone who copies others' actions or ideas, often a criminal mimicking another's crime.

clue.text: Restriction on moving vicious dog: not a lot

parts.note: a cur is a snappish, mongrel dog
few means not many

explanation.surface: A council notice restricting how a vicious dog may be moved, though not by much.
explanation.definitionFit: A curfew is an order keeping people indoors during set hours, limiting their freedom to go about.

clue.text: Father with beastly foot

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
W is a standard abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Dad is lumbered with a monstrous, ugly foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' looks like an insult, but it means belonging to a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A paw is the clawed or padded foot of an animal such as a dog or cat.

clue.text: Starchy bread modified to contain zero sugars etc

definitions.note: plural noun phrase, matching the plural answer

indicators.note: containing something means holding it within, so a letter is added inside the mix
something modified has been altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
O looks like the digit zero

explanation.surface: A recipe tweaks starchy bread so it carries no sugar at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of STARCHY BREAD plus O make up the thirteen-letter answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbohydrates are the nutrient class that includes sugars, starches and fibre, so sugars are examples of them.

clue.text: Arduous journey started regularly with kilometre

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of started
K is short for kilometre

explanation.surface: A tough hike that set off at a steady pace, one kilometre at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is a long, hard walk or expedition, often over difficult terrain.

clue.text: Small fish that's preserved for captain

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a kipper is a herring preserved by smoking

explanation.surface: A little smoked fish set aside for the ship's captain.
explanation.walkthrough: A kipper is a split, salted and smoked herring, a traditional British breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Skipper is the informal name for the captain of a boat or a sports team.

clue.text: Misery envelops empty rooms in less good condition

indicators.note: to envelop is to wrap around, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: woe is misery

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its insides, so only its outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of rooms

explanation.surface: Gloom settles over empty rooms in a house that is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' looks like a description of the rooms, but it tells you to discard their middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Worse is the comparative of bad, describing something that has deteriorated or is in a poorer state.

clue.text: Understanding feeling of dread

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the grasping of an idea
second meaning: anxiety about what is to come

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like one phrase, an understanding of dread, but splits into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the act of grasping something mentally and an anxious fear that something bad will happen.

clue.text: Witch captured by Venus or Ceres somehow

indicators.note: something captured by a group of words is held inside them, so the answer lies within the letters that follow

parts.note: the letters run from the last of Venus through or and Ceres into the first of somehow

explanation.surface: A witch has been seized by one of two Roman goddesses, though nobody quite knows how.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden word spans four words; the final word of the clue looks like an anagram signal but only lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorceress is a woman who practises magic or witchcraft, a female wizard.

clue.text: Big noise about unrefined allure

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: a din is a loud noise
raw means unprocessed or unrefined

explanation.surface: A loud fuss about some rough, untamed glamour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big noise' looks like an important person, but here it is just a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw in is to attract or entice people, just as to allure is to tempt them towards something.

clue.text: Beam in for every petition

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the first piece goes within the second

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A spotlight shone in for each request.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer is an earnest request, especially one addressed to God, so it is a form of plea or entreaty.

clue.text: Criticise show again

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to prove is to show or demonstrate

explanation.walkthrough: 'show' is used in the mathematical sense of demonstrating that something is true.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprove is to rebuke or tell someone off for a fault.

clue.text: One making a total season

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who sums, adding figures up
second meaning: the warmest time of the year

explanation.surface: Someone tallying up the whole season's results.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a jokey coinage: someone who sums is a 'summer'.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a person adding figures together and the hottest quarter of the year, between spring and autumn.

clue.text: Production of long-playing record?

parts.note: surface reading: a factory turning out an LP, a vinyl album
setter's reading: a stage production holding the record for the longest run in theatre history

explanation.walkthrough: Agatha Christie's murder mystery has run continuously in London's West End since 1952, the world's longest-running play.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christie play is a theatrical production famous for holding the record as the longest-running show.

clue.text: Enclosed area of a few feet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a walled patch of ground, as in a farmyard
second meaning: a length of three feet

explanation.surface: A small fenced space only a few feet across.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a fenced courtyard beside a building and an imperial measure equal to three feet.

clue.text: Monastery head's answer books: Old Testament

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
B is book, so BB is books
OT is the abbreviation for Old Testament

explanation.surface: The head of a monastery finds his answer in the books of the Old Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbot is the man in charge of an abbey or monastery of monks.

clue.text: Not quite the place for the dead cat

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a tomb is where the dead are laid

explanation.surface: A dead cat has nearly found its resting place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dead cat' reads as one phrase, but 'dead' belongs to the tomb and 'cat' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom is a male cat, short for tomcat.

clue.text: Conductor's ear, most refined

indicators.note: something refined has been reworked and processed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The orchestra conductor has the most discerning ear of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestro is an honorific for a distinguished musician, especially an orchestral conductor.

clue.text: I have visions, mostly dull, about myself

definitions.note: a self-description standing for the noun

indicators.note: about means around, so the shortened word wraps around the next piece
mostly means all but a little, so the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: dreary means dull and gloomy
me is myself

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that their visions are mostly dull and all about themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I have visions' is a first-person description standing in for the noun: the speaker is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamer is a person who sees visions while asleep or imagines grand ideals while awake.

clue.text: Girl's name that is introduced by South America

indicators.note: being introduced by others means they come first, so the later pieces precede this one

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south
US is short for the United States of America
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Her name, it turns out, was first heard from South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South America' looks like the continent, but it is two separate pieces, S and US.
explanation.definitionFit: Susie is a common female first name, a pet form of Susan or Susannah.
